chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a female slave who belongs to a woman, so she sells her: He said, 'There is no harm in him having intercourse with her without her being tested (istibra').'
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said, 'These two reports came absolutely (without condition), but the preferable course is to test her, which indicates that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on istibra' for a female slave sold by her owner?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of istibra' (waiting period to confirm pregnancy) for a female slave sold by her owner, establishing that while not legally mandatory for the buyer, it is recommended (afdhal) to ensure clarity of lineage. The text highlights the scholarly consensus on the preference for this precaution despite the absolute nature of the primary reports, reflecting the practical legal nuances in Shia jurisprudence regarding slave ownership and marital rights.
